//: Library source. `lib` includes DOM because the shared API client genuinely needs the standard fetch/Response/RequestInit types, which React Native also implements. It deliberately sets no `types`, so Node's globals (process, fs, Buffer) stay unavailable. DOM types unavoidably bring `window`/`document` into scope as well, which the compiler cannot separate from `fetch` — so the actual rule (no platform globals in shared code) is enforced by platformPurity.test.ts instead. Tests get Node's types via tsconfig.test.json so that allowance cannot leak here.
